case.case_title: Atukorale and Others v. T.P.F. De Silva - I.G.P. and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [1996] 1 Sri L.R. 280

clause.text: All persons are equal before the law and are entitled to the equal protection of the law.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the refusal by the 1st Respondent to allow the UNP May Day rally and procession in Kandy violated the Petitioners' right to equality before the law under Article 12(1) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The Petitioners claimed that the refusal to permit their May Day rally and procession in Kandy was arbitrary, capricious, and discriminatory, violating their right to equality before the law as they were treated differently from other political parties allowed to hold rallies in other towns.
case_context.respondent_argument: The 1st Respondent argued that permission was refused due to security, logistical, and administrative imperatives, and that the Petitioners had not made a formal application. He also contended that other smaller parties were permitted to hold rallies in provinces because they had a long-standing geographical base there, whereas major parties held celebrations in the city.
key_facts: The UNP requested permission to hold a May Day rally and procession in Kandy, specifically at the Central Bus Stand and along a specified route.
Permission was refused by the 1st Respondent citing security, logistical, and administrative reasons without detailed explanation.
Permission was granted to four other political parties, all constituent parties of the Peoples Alliance, to hold rallies in other towns.
The Petitioners alleged discrimination based on political opinion and unequal treatment compared to other parties.
The 1st Respondent offered alternative venues (Bogambara Grounds parking area and Colombo) which the Petitioners rejected.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court interpreted Article 12(1) as guaranteeing equality before the law and equal protection, requiring that any differential treatment must be justified and not arbitrary or discriminatory.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found that the 1st Respondent failed to provide sufficient explanation or justification for refusing permission to the Petitioners while allowing other parties to hold rallies, indicating unequal treatment. The lack of substantiation for the security and logistical reasons and the acceptance of other parties' rallies in provinces demonstrated discrimination.
principles_established: Refusal of permission without valid and explained grounds violates the right to equality before the law.
Differential treatment based on political opinion constitutes discrimination under Article 12(2).
Authorities must provide clear and reasonable grounds when restricting fundamental rights.

outcome.holding: The court held that there was a violation of the Petitioners' right to equality before the law under Article 12(1) of the Constitution.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The determination and/or order refusing permission to hold the May Day meeting and procession in Kandy was quashed, and costs were awarded to the Petitioners.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(1) was central to the court's finding that the Petitioners were treated unequally and that the refusal to permit their rally was arbitrary and unjustified, thus violating their fundamental rights.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court found that the 1st Respondent failed to explain the security, logistical, and administrative constraints and that permission was granted to other parties in other towns, constituting discrimination and violation of Article 12(1).
